title: Kidney-expressed blood pressure predicted effector genes (Eales et al. 2021)
bodyHtml:
This table displays evidence for 179 kidney-expressed genes with putatively causal effects on blood pressure, from the study:

Uncovering genetic mechanisms of hypertension through multi-omic analysis of the kidney.
Eales JM, Jiang X, Xu X, et al.
Nat Genet. 2021 May;53(5):630-637. doi: 10.1038/s41588-021-00835-w.
PMID: 33958779

In this study, the authors performed cis-eQTL, cis-sQTL, and cis-mQTL analysis, using 430 human kidney samples collected after elective nephrectomies or before renal transplantation, to identify SNPs associated with gene expression, splicing, and methylation, respectively, in the kidney.

The authors defined the set of SNPs that were genetically associated with systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and/or pulse pressure as the sentinel SNPs and their proxies (under the threshold of r2 ≥ 0.80) identified in a recent large blood pressure GWAS (Evangelou et al., 2018); the associations from the discovery analysis, meta-analysis, and combined meta-analysis were considered.

They then used the moloc software package (Giambartolomei et al., 2018) to determine colocalization of molecular QTL SNPs with GWAS SNPs, and performed two-sample Mendelian Randomization to uncover causal evidence of association of molecular QTLs and their target genes with blood pressure.

They also searched the literature and public databases to gather additional evidence for roles of the prioritized genes in kidney physiology and blood pressure regulation.
